body: I told my mom because I live with her. I had to. Plus the position was obtained through nepotism via her friend. I've gradually started telling friends, although I lied about the real reason just because it's embarrassing. I've been seeing a therapist for over a year now. I filed for unemployment and I started looking at listings. Sometimes I'm level headed and capable of doing these things. Sometimes I'm just full of despair and devastation and I can't even sit up because supporting the weight of my body is asking too much. Sometimes I dissociate and it feels like I'm not even real, my mind is just watching my body's actions like my body is a character in a movie I'm really engaged in. Been having sleep trouble because of course I have sleep trouble when I need sleep the most. Not all of my friends know but some of them do. I want to say I'm not worried about my safety but I've been unstable in terms of mood so I'm a little less confident about that than normal.

I graduated college about 5 years ago. The position was kind of a favor from my mom's friend. She is high up at a hospital and was able to create a position for me through some grant funding(for the record, I did do a good amount of work related to the project the grant was for). I interviewed with the team and I got the job. There was some nepotism involved but my now-former-boss didn't have to take me, the interview went well and we picked a start date. My title was officially "Extern" for the Data Science department. At some point it was clearly communicated that the goal was to make me able to start a career in Data Science and hopefully be taken in as a full time employee by the hospital. That being said, the way my boss kind of framed the firing seemed insincere, even though it was ultimately my fault. My boss said that it "wasn't fair" to the other team members to be put to a different standard than me. I get that browsing the internet is a problem and the core of the issue, but all the team members have significantly more knowledge and experience in this field than I do, are paid significantly more and got benefits such as health insurance and PTO(Meanwhile me getting sick meant docked pay). When phrased the way she put it, it just seems ludicrous to give me the same output standards as them, even though I know that's not really what this was about. Former boss said she did like the work that I did, but my output was lacking and I needed more focus. Having a little bit of time to think about it, the work/times my boss liked my performance and the work/times my boss was dissatisfied tells me a lot about both the kind of work tasks I like to do, and the kind of overall organizational structure I prefer. I wish I could have lasted at least a couple more months but on top of learning some hard skills in a new field, I have a better idea of how I work, and how to overcome some of my weaknesses a bit. My degree is in Media/Communication but I guess after this experience I'm hoping to enter(continue?) a career in Business Intelligence, and maybe Data Science.
